# Kalaa (@kalaa/react v0.3.0)

> Calm, accessible React components, data-driven blocks and full-page templates styled with Kalaa design tokens (`--kalaa-*`). Square by default (`data-shape="soft"` for rounded corners), three Indian-pigment accents (`neel`, `geru`, `mayur`), light and dark themes (`data-theme="light|dark"`), and A4/Letter black-on-white print stylesheets.

## Data-first AI workflow

1. Validate or populate a single JSON object conforming to `ResumeData` (`@kalaa/react/resume.schema.json`) or `PortfolioData` (`@kalaa/react/portfolio.schema.json`).
2. Pass the data object to `<ResumePage data={resumeData} layout="single-column" />`, `<PortfolioPage data={portfolioData} />`, or `<LandingPage data={landingPageData} />`.
3. Compose custom views from individual blocks in `Blocks/Resume`, `Blocks/Profile & portfolio`, `Blocks/Marketing`, and primitives in `Components`.

## Exported JSON Schemas and helpers

- `ResumeData`, `resumeDataSchema`, `validateResumeData`, `sampleResumeData` (`@kalaa/react/resume.schema.json`)
- `PortfolioData`, `portfolioDataSchema`, `validatePortfolioData`, `samplePortfolioData` (`@kalaa/react/portfolio.schema.json`)
- `LandingPageData`, `sampleLandingPageData`

## Templates

### ResumePage

Complete web and print resume template driven by a single `ResumeData` JSON object. Provides `"single-column"` and `"sidebar"` layouts, A4 and US Letter sizing, ATS-linear DOM order and automatic black-on-white print output even in dark mode.

Props:
- `data` (`ResumeData`, required) — Complete JSON-serialisable resume data object conforming to `ResumeData`.
- `layout` (`ResumePageLayout`, optional, default: "single-column") — Page layout: "single-column" (linear ATS flow, default) or "sidebar" (two-column print/web layout).
- `paperSize` (`ResumePaperSize`, optional, default: "a4") — Target print paper geometry: "a4" (210mm, default) or "letter" (8.5in).
- `forcePrintPreview` (`boolean`, optional, default: false) — Forces black-on-white print tokens on screen (useful for previewing print output in dark mode).

Example:
```tsx
import { ResumePage, sampleResumeData } from "@kalaa/react";

<ResumePage data={sampleResumeData} layout="single-column" paperSize="a4" />
```

### PortfolioPage

Complete personal portfolio page template driven by a single `PortfolioData` JSON object. Composes `ProfileCard`, `CaseStudyCard`, `ProjectList`, `Timeline`, `SkillGroups`, `TestimonialCard`, `LinkList`, `ContactCard` and `PageFooter` with semantic landmarks.

Props:
- `data` (`PortfolioData`, required) — Complete JSON-serialisable portfolio data object conforming to `PortfolioData`.

Example:
```tsx
import { PortfolioPage, samplePortfolioData } from "@kalaa/react";

<PortfolioPage data={samplePortfolioData} />
```

### LandingPage

Complete product and marketing landing page template driven by a single `LandingPageData` JSON object. Composes `Hero`, `StatsBand`, `FeatureGrid`, `TestimonialCard`, `FAQ`, `CTA` and `PageFooter` with accessible landmarks.

Props:
- `data` (`LandingPageData`, required) — Complete JSON-serialisable marketing page data object conforming to `LandingPageData`.

Example:
```tsx
import { LandingPage, sampleLandingPageData } from "@kalaa/react";

<LandingPage data={sampleLandingPageData} />
```

## Blocks/Resume

### ResumeHeader

Top identity block for a web or print resume with candidate name (`h1`), professional title, location and contact links.

Props:
- `name` (`string`, required) — Candidate full name (rendered as `h1`).
- `title` (`string`, required) — Primary professional title or headline.
- `location` (`string`, optional) — City, region or timezone.
- `email` (`string`, optional) — Contact email address.
- `phone` (`string`, optional) — Contact phone number.
- `website` (`string`, optional) — Personal website URL.
- `links` (`ResumeContactLink[]`, optional, default: []) — Additional profile or portfolio links.
- `badge` (`string`, optional) — Optional availability or status label shown in a badge.

Example:
```tsx
import { ResumeHeader } from "@kalaa/react";

<ResumeHeader
  name="Aarav Deshmukh"
  title="Principal Systems Architect"
  location="Pune, India"
  email="aarav.deshmukh@example.invalid"
/>
```

### Summary

Executive summary block with a section heading, concise narrative paragraph and optional bulleted highlights.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Summary") — Section heading text (default "Summary").
- `text` (`string`, required) — Primary summary paragraph.
- `highlights` (`string[]`, optional, default: []) — Optional factual highlights shown as a bulleted list.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Heading level (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { Summary } from "@kalaa/react";

<Summary
  text="Systems architect with 11 years designing deterministic telemetry pipelines."
  highlights={["Cut regional failover recovery from 14 minutes to 22 seconds"]}
/>
```

### ExperienceList

Chronological work history block composed of `ExperienceItem` entries with role, organisation, semantic `<time>` dates, outcome bullets and technology `Badge` tags.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Experience") — Section heading (default "Experience").
- `items` (`ResumeExperienceItem[]`, required) — Chronological experience entries.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2; items render one level deeper).

Example:
```tsx
import { ExperienceList } from "@kalaa/react";

<ExperienceList
  items={[
    {
      role: "Principal Systems Architect",
      org: "Vayu Grid Systems",
      startDate: "2023-04",
      endDate: "Present",
      bullets: ["Sustained 1.4M events/s at p99 latency under 18 ms."],
      tags: ["Rust", "Go", "TypeScript"],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### ExperienceItem

Chronological work history block composed of `ExperienceItem` entries with role, organisation, semantic `<time>` dates, outcome bullets and technology `Badge` tags.

Props:
- `role` (`string`, required) — Job title or role name.
- `org` (`string`, required) — Company or organisation name.
- `location` (`string`, optional) — City, region or remote status.
- `startDate` (`string`, required) — ISO or human-readable start date (rendered inside `<time>`).
- `endDate` (`string`, optional, default: "Present") — ISO or human-readable end date, or "Present" if current.
- `summary` (`string`, optional) — Optional one-line role overview.
- `bullets` (`string[]`, required) — Impact bullets in sentence case.
- `tags` (`string[]`, optional, default: []) — Technology or domain tags shown as badges.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3 | 4`, optional, default: 2) — Heading level for the role title (default 2 when standalone, 3 inside ExperienceList).

Example:
```tsx
import { ExperienceList } from "@kalaa/react";

<ExperienceList
  items={[
    {
      role: "Principal Systems Architect",
      org: "Vayu Grid Systems",
      startDate: "2023-04",
      endDate: "Present",
      bullets: ["Sustained 1.4M events/s at p99 latency under 18 ms."],
      tags: ["Rust", "Go", "TypeScript"],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### EducationList

Academic qualifications block showing degrees, institutions, graduation `<time>` dates, thesis notes and honours badges.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Education") — Section heading (default "Education").
- `items` (`ResumeEducationItem[]`, required) — Academic credentials list.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2; degree titles render one level deeper).

Example:
```tsx
import { EducationList } from "@kalaa/react";

<EducationList
  items={[
    {
      degree: "M.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering",
      institution: "Visvesvaraya Institute of Technology",
      startDate: "2014",
      endDate: "2016",
      honors: ["Institute Gold Medal"],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### SkillGroups

Categorised skill groups rendered inside a semantic `<dl>` with Kalaa `Badge` items. Supports responsive `"grid"` or narrow `"stacked"` sidebar layouts.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Skills") — Section heading (default "Skills").
- `groups` (`ResumeSkillGroup[]`, required) — Categorised skill groups.
- `layout` (`"grid" | "stacked"`, optional, default: "grid") — Visual arrangement: "grid" (default) or "stacked" for narrow sidebars.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { SkillGroups } from "@kalaa/react";

<SkillGroups
  groups={[
    { category: "Systems & backend", skills: ["Rust", "Go", "TypeScript", "PostgreSQL"] },
  ]}
/>
```

### ProjectList

Grid or stack of `ProjectCard` blocks built on Kalaa `Card`, `KeyValue` and `Badge` with impact numbers, technology tags and links.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Projects") — Section heading (default "Projects").
- `items` (`ResumeProjectItem[]`, required) — Project entries to render.
- `columns` (`1 | 2`, optional, default: 2) — Number of columns on wide screens (default 2).
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2; project titles render one level deeper).

Example:
```tsx
import { ProjectList } from "@kalaa/react";

<ProjectList
  items={[
    {
      name: "Pravah Stream Compactor",
      description: "Time-series segment compactor for edge gateways.",
      impact: [{ label: "Write amplification", value: "1.18x (-54%)" }],
      tags: ["Rust", "Storage"],
      links: [{ label: "Source", href: "https://github.example.invalid/vayu-grid/pravah" }],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### ProjectCard

Grid or stack of `ProjectCard` blocks built on Kalaa `Card`, `KeyValue` and `Badge` with impact numbers, technology tags and links.

Props:
- `name` (`string`, required) — Project name.
- `description` (`string`, required) — Concise explanation of what was built and why.
- `role` (`string`, optional) — Optional role on the project.
- `startDate` (`string`, optional) — Start date or year.
- `endDate` (`string`, optional) — End date or year.
- `impact` (`ResumeProjectImpact[]`, optional, default: []) — Quantified outcomes and impact metrics.
- `tags` (`string[]`, optional, default: []) — Technology tags.
- `links` (`ResumeContactLink[]`, optional, default: []) — External links (repository, live demo, paper).
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3 | 4`, optional, default: 2) — Heading level for the project title (default 2 when standalone, 3 inside ProjectList).

Example:
```tsx
import { ProjectList } from "@kalaa/react";

<ProjectList
  items={[
    {
      name: "Pravah Stream Compactor",
      description: "Time-series segment compactor for edge gateways.",
      impact: [{ label: "Write amplification", value: "1.18x (-54%)" }],
      tags: ["Rust", "Storage"],
      links: [{ label: "Source", href: "https://github.example.invalid/vayu-grid/pravah" }],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### Certifications

Professional certifications block with issuer name, `<time>` dates, optional verification link and credential ID `Badge`.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Certifications") — Section heading (default "Certifications").
- `items` (`ResumeCertificationItem[]`, required) — Certification entries.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { Certifications } from "@kalaa/react";

<Certifications
  items={[
    {
      name: "Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS)",
      issuer: "Cloud Native Computing Foundation",
      date: "2024-02",
      credentialId: "CNCF-CKS-884120",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### Languages

Spoken and written languages block pairing each language name with a proficiency `Badge`.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Languages") — Section heading (default "Languages").
- `items` (`ResumeLanguageItem[]`, required) — Spoken or written languages with proficiency labels.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { Languages } from "@kalaa/react";

<Languages
  items={[
    { language: "Marathi", proficiency: "Native or bilingual", level: "native" },
    { language: "English", proficiency: "Full professional proficiency", level: "fluent" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Awards

Honours, awards and peer-reviewed publications list (`Awards` and `Publications`) with `<time>` dates, issuer details and category `Badge`.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Awards & publications") — Section heading (default "Awards & publications").
- `items` (`ResumeAwardItem[]`, required) — Award and publication entries.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2; entry titles render one level deeper).

Example:
```tsx
import { Awards } from "@kalaa/react";

<Awards
  items={[
    {
      title: "National Grid Resilience Engineering Award",
      issuer: "Indian Power Systems Forum",
      date: "2024-11",
      kind: "award",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### Publications

Honours, awards and peer-reviewed publications list (`Awards` and `Publications`) with `<time>` dates, issuer details and category `Badge`.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Publications") — Section heading (default "Awards & publications").
- `items` (`ResumeAwardItem[]`, required) — Award and publication entries.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional) — Section heading level (default 2; entry titles render one level deeper).

Example:
```tsx
import { Awards } from "@kalaa/react";

<Awards
  items={[
    {
      title: "National Grid Resilience Engineering Award",
      issuer: "Indian Power Systems Forum",
      date: "2024-11",
      kind: "award",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

## Blocks/Profile & portfolio

### ProfileCard

Personal identity and bio card with monogram avatar, availability `Badge`, tabular-figure stats, skill tags and `ButtonLink` actions (at most one primary).

Props:
- `name` (`string`, required) — Person's full name.
- `role` (`string`, required) — Primary role or headline.
- `location` (`string`, optional) — Location or timezone.
- `bio` (`string`, required) — Short biography paragraph.
- `availability` (`string`, optional) — Availability status (for example "Available for architecture reviews").
- `initials` (`string`, optional) — Avatar monogram initials (for example "AD").
- `skills` (`string[]`, optional, default: []) — Top skill tags.
- `stats` (`PortfolioStat[]`, optional, default: []) — Career highlight numbers.
- `primaryAction` (`PortfolioAction`, optional) — Primary action link.
- `secondaryAction` (`PortfolioAction`, optional) — Secondary action link.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Heading level for the person's name (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { ProfileCard } from "@kalaa/react";

<ProfileCard
  name="Aarav Deshmukh"
  role="Principal Systems Architect"
  bio="I design high-throughput telemetry engines and calm operator consoles."
  availability="Available for Q1 reviews"
/>
```

### CaseStudyCard

Portfolio case study card built on Kalaa `Card`, `KeyValue`, `Badge` and `ButtonLink` with structured Challenge/Outcome rows and `<time>` year.

Props:
- `title` (`string`, required) — Case study title.
- `client` (`string`, optional) — Client or organisation name.
- `year` (`string`, required) — Year or date completed.
- `summary` (`string`, required) — Overview of the engagement.
- `challenge` (`string`, optional) — Key problem addressed.
- `outcome` (`string`, optional) — Result delivered.
- `metrics` (`ResumeProjectImpact[]`, optional, default: []) — Quantified impact metrics.
- `tags` (`string[]`, optional, default: []) — Domain or technology tags.
- `href` (`string`, optional) — Link to full write-up.
- `ctaLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "Read case study") — Link button label.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3 | 4`, optional, default: 2) — Heading level for the case study title (default 2 when standalone, 3 inside a section).

Example:
```tsx
import { CaseStudyCard } from "@kalaa/react";

<CaseStudyCard
  title="Substation telemetry pipeline overhaul"
  client="Vayu Grid Systems"
  year="2025"
  summary="Replaced a polling collector with a bounded-memory Rust stream compactor."
  metrics={[{ label: "Recovery time", value: "22 s" }]}
/>
```

### Timeline

Chronological milestone list rendered as a semantic `<ol>` with `<time>` dates, role/project titles, subtitles and `Badge` tags.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Timeline") — Optional section heading (default "Timeline").
- `items` (`PortfolioTimelineItem[]`, required) — Chronological milestones.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2; milestone titles render one level deeper).

Example:
```tsx
import { Timeline } from "@kalaa/react";

<Timeline
  items={[
    {
      date: "2023-04",
      endDate: "Present",
      title: "Principal Systems Architect",
      subtitle: "Vayu Grid Systems",
      badge: "Current",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### TestimonialCard

Endorsement card built on Kalaa `Card` (`as="article"`) with a semantic `<blockquote>`, `<cite>` author attribution, role, organisation and `<time>` date.

Props:
- `quote` (`string`, required) — Verbatim testimonial text.
- `author` (`string`, required) — Full name of the person quoted.
- `role` (`string`, required) — Author's job title.
- `org` (`string`, optional) — Author's company or organisation.
- `date` (`string`, optional) — Date or year of the endorsement.
- `context` (`string`, optional) — Relationship or project context.

Example:
```tsx
import { TestimonialCard } from "@kalaa/react";

<TestimonialCard
  quote="Aarav turned our most fragile telemetry service into the calmest part of our stack."
  author="Meera Kulkarni"
  role="VP of Engineering"
  org="Vayu Grid Systems"
/>
```

### ContactCard

Direct contact card built on Kalaa `Card`, `KeyValue`, `Badge` and `ButtonLink` with email, location, response time and a primary `mailto:` action.

Props:
- `title` (`string`, optional, default: "Get in touch") — Heading for the contact card.
- `description` (`string`, optional) — Invitation copy below the heading.
- `email` (`string`, required) — Contact email address.
- `phone` (`string`, optional) — Optional phone number.
- `location` (`string`, optional) — City, country or timezone.
- `availability` (`string`, optional) — Current availability window.
- `responseTime` (`string`, optional) — Typical response time.
- `ctaLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "Send email") — Primary email button label.
- `links` (`ResumeContactLink[]`, optional, default: []) — Additional profile links.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3 | 4`, optional, default: 2) — Heading level for the card title (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { ContactCard } from "@kalaa/react";

<ContactCard
  title="Start a technical conversation"
  email="aarav.deshmukh@example.invalid"
  location="Pune, India"
  responseTime="Within 1 business day"
/>
```

### LinkList

Annotated link collection for writing, talks, repositories or profile hubs. Supports `"stacked"` rows with descriptions or compact `"inline"` rows.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional) — Optional section heading.
- `items` (`PortfolioLinkItem[]`, required) — Annotated links to render.
- `variant` (`"stacked" | "inline"`, optional, default: "stacked") — Visual variant: "stacked" (default, with descriptions) or "inline" (compact horizontal bar).
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { LinkList } from "@kalaa/react";

<LinkList
  heading="Selected writing"
  items={[
    {
      label: "Deterministic rollup compaction paper",
      href: "https://papers.example.invalid/sits-2025-rollup",
      description: "Symposium on Industrial Telemetry Systems (2025)",
      meta: "Paper",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

## Blocks/Marketing

### Hero

Top marketing hero block with optional release `Badge`, IBM Plex Serif `h1` headline, value proposition, `ButtonLink` actions (one primary, one secondary) and factual highlights.

Props:
- `eyebrow` (`string`, optional) — Optional badge label above the title.
- `title` (`string`, required) — Primary headline.
- `description` (`string`, required) — Supporting value proposition paragraph.
- `primaryAction` (`PortfolioAction`, optional) — Main call-to-action button.
- `secondaryAction` (`PortfolioAction`, optional) — Secondary link button.
- `highlights` (`string[]`, optional, default: []) — Short factual highlights below the actions.
- `align` (`"start" | "center"`, optional, default: "start") — Content alignment: "start" (default) or "center".
- `headingLevel` (`1 | 2`, optional, default: 1) — Heading level for the hero title (default 1).

Example:
```tsx
import { Hero } from "@kalaa/react";

<Hero
  eyebrow="Release 2.4"
  title="Calm telemetry for high-voltage operations"
  description="Ingest, compact and inspect millions of sensor events per second."
  primaryAction={{ label: "Deploy sample cluster", href: "#cta" }}
/>
```

### FeatureGrid

Responsive 2- or 3-column grid of product capabilities built from `SectionHeader`, Kalaa `Card` and `Badge`.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional) — Section heading.
- `description` (`string`, optional) — Supporting section description.
- `features` (`LandingFeatureItem[]`, required) — Feature items rendered as Kalaa `Card` blocks.
- `columns` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 3) — Number of columns on desktop (default 3).
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2; feature cards render one level deeper when heading is set).

Example:
```tsx
import { FeatureGrid } from "@kalaa/react";

<FeatureGrid
  heading="Engineered for predictable operations"
  features={[
    {
      title: "Bounded-memory stream compactor",
      description: "Fixed ring buffers guarantee zero out-of-memory restarts.",
      badge: "Storage",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### StatsBand

Horizontal benchmark and KPI band rendering figures with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` inside a semantic `<dl>`.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional) — Optional section heading.
- `description` (`string`, optional) — Optional supporting description.
- `stats` (`PortfolioStat[]`, required) — Key metrics rendered with tabular numerals.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { StatsBand } from "@kalaa/react";

<StatsBand
  heading="Measured under real substation fault bursts"
  stats={[
    { label: "Ingest throughput", value: "1.4M/s", detail: "Per 4-core regional node" },
    { label: "Failover recovery", value: "22 s", detail: "Zero dropped frames" },
  ]}
/>
```

### CTA

Call-to-action card with a 3px accent start border, serif heading, description, optional note and `ButtonLink` actions.

Props:
- `title` (`string`, required) — Action heading.
- `description` (`string`, optional) — Supporting explanation.
- `primaryAction` (`PortfolioAction`, required) — Primary action link.
- `secondaryAction` (`PortfolioAction`, optional) — Optional secondary action link.
- `note` (`string`, optional) — Optional note below the buttons.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Heading level (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { CTA } from "@kalaa/react";

<CTA
  title="Ready to calm your telemetry stack?"
  description="Run the self-contained simulator locally."
  primaryAction={{ label: "Download evaluation tarball", href: "#download" }}
/>
```

### FAQ

Frequently asked questions block built on native HTML `<details>` and `<summary>` elements so disclosures work without client-side JavaScript.

Props:
- `heading` (`string`, optional, default: "Frequently asked questions") — Section heading (default "Frequently asked questions").
- `description` (`string`, optional) — Optional supporting description.
- `items` (`LandingFaqItem[]`, required) — Question and answer pairs rendered as native `<details>` disclosures.
- `defaultOpenAll` (`boolean`, optional, default: false) — Opens all items by default (also ensures full answer visibility when printing).
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Section heading level (default 2).

Example:
```tsx
import { FAQ } from "@kalaa/react";

<FAQ
  items={[
    {
      question: "Does the operator console work without client-side JavaScript?",
      answer: "Yes. Every report and disclosure renders valid semantic HTML on the server.",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### PageFooter

Semantic `<footer>` landmark with the Kalaa `LogoMark`, brand tagline, uniquely labelled `<nav>` link columns and utility links.

Props:
- `brandName` (`string`, required) — Brand or owner name.
- `tagline` (`string`, optional) — Short tagline below the brand.
- `columns` (`PortfolioFooterColumn[]`, optional, default: []) — Structured link columns.
- `links` (`ResumeContactLink[]`, optional, default: []) — Flat utility links.
- `copyright` (`string`, optional) — Copyright or licence line.
- `showLogo` (`boolean`, optional, default: true) — Whether to render the Kalaa mark next to the brand name.

Example:
```tsx
import { PageFooter } from "@kalaa/react";

<PageFooter
  brandName="Pravah Telemetry"
  tagline="Built with Kalaa design tokens and components."
  copyright="© 2026 Pravah Telemetry Systems."
/>
```

### SectionHeader

Consistent section heading (`h2` or `h3`) with an optional `Badge`, muted description and secondary `ButtonLink` action.

Props:
- `title` (`string`, required) — Section heading text.
- `description` (`string`, optional) — Supporting description below the heading.
- `badge` (`string`, optional) — Optional status or category badge text.
- `action` (`PortfolioAction`, optional) — Optional secondary action link on the right.
- `headingLevel` (`2 | 3`, optional, default: 2) — Heading level (default 2).
- `align` (`"between" | "start"`, optional, default: "between") — Horizontal alignment: "between" (default) or "start".

Example:
```tsx
import { SectionHeader } from "@kalaa/react";

<SectionHeader
  title="Engineered for predictable operations"
  description="Every layer is inspectable, schema-validated and operable from the keyboard."
/>
```

## Components

### AppShell

Page frame with a sticky 240px sidebar (full-page background) and a main area (max 1120px). Use it once per app, with `brand`, `AppShell.NavItem` children in `nav`, and `footer` for account or theme utilities. Pass `render={<NextLink href="..." />}` on `NavItem` for client-side routing.

Props:
- `nav` (`ReactNode`, required) — Sidebar content, usually `AppShell.NavItem` links.
- `header` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Optional content above the main area (for example a page header).
- `brand` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Brand slot at the top of the sidebar (logo, app name). Stays beside the Menu button on small screens.
- `footer` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Footer or utility slot at the bottom of the sidebar (theme toggle, account, sign out).

Example:
```tsx
import NextLink from "next/link";
import { AppShell } from "@kalaa/react";

<AppShell
  brand="Catalog Admin"
  nav={<AppShell.NavItem render={<NextLink href="/products" />} active>Products</AppShell.NavItem>}
  footer={<button type="button">Sign out</button>}
>
  <PageHeader title="Products" />
</AppShell>
```

### PageHeader

Title row for a page: optional back link, one `h1`, muted description and right-aligned actions. Pass `back={{ href, label, render: <NextLink href="..." /> }}` for client-side routing in Next.js.

Props:
- `title` (`ReactNode`, required) — The page `h1`.
- `description` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Muted line under the title.
- `back` (`{ href: string; label: string; render?: useRender.RenderProp; }`, optional) — Link above the title to the parent page.
- `actions` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Buttons on the right of the title row; at most one primary.
- `variant` (`"default" | "brand"`, optional, default: "default") — "brand" sets the title in serif for marketing pages.

Example:
```tsx
import NextLink from "next/link";
import { PageHeader, Button } from "@kalaa/react";

<PageHeader
  title="Products"
  description="Manage your catalog."
  back={{ href: "/catalog", label: "Back to catalog", render: <NextLink href="/catalog" /> }}
  actions={<Button variant="primary">Add product</Button>}
/>
```

### Card

Bordered surface that groups related content. A header row appears only when there is a title or actions.

Props:
- `as` (`"section" | "div" | "article"`, optional, default: "section") — Root element (default section).
- `title` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Card heading.
- `description` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Muted line under the title.
- `actions` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Content on the right of the header row.
- `titleLevel` (`2 | 3 | 4`, optional, default: 2) — Heading level of the title (default 2). Use 3 or 4 when the card sits under a section heading.

Example:
```tsx
import { Card } from "@kalaa/react";

<Card title="Products" description="Manage your catalog.">24 products</Card>
```

### KeyValue

Definition list for facts about one thing. `rows` has a label column and dividers; `grid` fits summaries.

Props:
- `items` (`Array<{ label: ReactNode; value: ReactNode }>`, required) — Label and value pairs; an empty value shows an em dash.
- `layout` (`"rows" | "grid"`, optional, default: "rows") — "rows" (label column with dividers, default) or "grid" (compact summary).

Example:
```tsx
import { KeyValue } from "@kalaa/react";

<KeyValue items={[{ label: "Status", value: "Draft" }, { label: "Stock", value: "88 units" }]} />
```

### ValueComparison

Compare an original value with a proposed value. Panels stack when their container is narrow. Set a contextual accessible name when showing multiple comparisons and use a separate control for accepting a proposal.

Props:
- `original` (`ReactNode`, required)
- `proposed` (`ReactNode`, required)
- `originalLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "Original")
- `proposedLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "Proposed")
- `emptyLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "No value")

Example:
```tsx
import { ValueComparison } from "@kalaa/react";

<ValueComparison />
```

### EmptyState

Centred message for a list or area with nothing in it, with one optional next step.

Props:
- `title` (`ReactNode`, required) — What is missing, for example "No products yet".
- `description` (`ReactNode`, optional) — What to do about it.
- `action` (`ReactNode`, optional) — One next step, usually a Button.

Example:
```tsx
import { EmptyState } from "@kalaa/react";

<EmptyState title="No products yet" description="Add a product to start your catalog." />
```

### Button

Action button. `primary` is the main next step, `secondary` the default, `ghost` low-emphasis inline actions, `danger` destructive ones.

Props:
- `variant` (`ButtonVariant`, optional, default: "secondary") — primary (main next step), secondary (default), ghost (low emphasis) or danger (destructive).
- `size` (`ButtonSize`, optional, default: "md") — Height: sm 30px, md 36px (default).
- `iconStart` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Decorative icon before the label.
- `iconEnd` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Decorative icon after the label.
- `loading` (`boolean`, optional, default: false) — Shows a spinner, disables the button and sets `aria-busy`; keeps its width.

Example:
```tsx
import { Button } from "@kalaa/react";

<Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>
```

### ButtonLink

A link that looks like a Button, for navigation. Same variants and sizes; works with any router through `href` or the Base UI `render` prop (for example `next/link`).

Props:
- `variant` (`ButtonVariant`, optional, default: "secondary") — primary (main next step), secondary (default), ghost (low emphasis) or danger (destructive).
- `size` (`ButtonSize`, optional, default: "md") — Height: sm 30px, md 36px (default).
- `iconStart` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Decorative icon before the label.
- `iconEnd` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Decorative icon after the label.
- `render` (`useRender.RenderProp`, optional) — Replaces the `<a>` element, for client-side routing. Pass your router's link, for example `render={<NextLink href="/products" />}` with `next/link`. Kalaa props and classes are merged onto it.

Example:
```tsx
import NextLink from "next/link";
import { ButtonLink } from "@kalaa/react";

<ButtonLink variant="primary" render={<NextLink href="/products" />}>
  View products
</ButtonLink>
```

### Field

Wraps one control with a label, optional hint, error and required marker, and wires `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`.

Props:
- `label` (`ReactNode`, required) — Visible label above the control, in sentence case.
- `hint` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Help text below the control.
- `error` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Error message; marks the control invalid.
- `required` (`boolean`, optional) — Adds "(required)" to the label.
- `children` (`ReactElement<ControlProps>`, required) — Exactly one control (Input, Textarea, Select).

Example:
```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@kalaa/react";

<Field label="Product title" hint="Shown on the storefront.">
  <Input defaultValue="Cold-pressed mustard oil 1 L" />
</Field>
```

### Input

Single-line text input (native props plus `size` and `invalid`). Put it in a `Field` to get a label and error text.

Props:
- `size` (`"sm" | "md"`, optional, default: "md") — Height: sm 30px, md 36px (default).
- `invalid` (`boolean`, optional) — Shows the danger border and sets `aria-invalid`.

Example:
```tsx
import { Input } from "@kalaa/react";

<Input aria-label="Product name" placeholder="Enter product name" />
```

### Textarea

Multi-line text input with the same look as Input; `autoResize` grows it with its content.

Props:
- `size` (`"sm" | "md"`, optional, default: "md") — Text size and padding: sm or md (default).
- `invalid` (`boolean`, optional) — Shows the danger border and sets `aria-invalid`.
- `autoResize` (`boolean`, optional) — Grows with its content instead of scrolling.

Example:
```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@kalaa/react";

<Textarea aria-label="Product description" autoResize />
```

### Select

Dropdown built on Base UI Select, with keyboard support (arrows, type-ahead, Escape).

Props:
- `options` (`SelectOption[]`, required) — Choices as value and label pairs.
- `value` (`string`, optional) — Controlled value.
- `defaultValue` (`string`, optional) — Initial value when uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange` (`(value: string | null) => void`, optional) — Called with the new value.
- `placeholder` (`string`, optional, default: "Select an option") — Text shown when nothing is selected.
- `size` (`"sm" | "md"`, optional, default: "md") — Height: sm 30px, md 36px (default).
- `invalid` (`boolean`, optional) — Shows the danger border and sets `aria-invalid`.
- `name` (`string`, optional) — Form field name.
- `required` (`boolean`, optional) — Marks the field required in forms.

Example:
```tsx
import { Select } from "@kalaa/react";

<Select
  aria-label="Review status"
  options={[{ value: "draft", label: "Draft" }, { value: "review", label: "Needs review" }]}
  defaultValue="draft"
/>
```

### Checkbox

Checkbox with a label and optional description, built on Base UI. Supports `indeterminate` for select all.

Props:
- `label` (`ReactNode`, required) — Visible label, shown to the right of the box.
- `description` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Optional help text under the label, linked with `aria-describedby`.
- `className` (`string`, optional)

Example:
```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@kalaa/react";

<Checkbox label="Show on storefront" defaultChecked />
```

### Switch

On/off setting that applies immediately, with a label and optional description.

Props:
- `label` (`ReactNode`, required) — Visible label, shown to the right of the switch.
- `description` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Optional help text under the label, linked with `aria-describedby`.
- `className` (`string`, optional)

Example:
```tsx
import { Switch } from "@kalaa/react";

<Switch label="Track stock" description="Warn when fewer than 20 units are left." />
```

### Tabs

Switches between views of one subject. `segmented` for compact filters, `underline` for page sections.

Props:
- `items` (`TabItem[]`, required) — Tabs with their panel content.
- `value` (`string`, optional) — Controlled selected tab.
- `defaultValue` (`string`, optional) — Initially selected tab when uncontrolled (default: first enabled).
- `onValueChange` (`(value: string) => void`, optional) — Called with the selected tab value.
- `variant` (`"segmented" | "underline"`, optional, default: "segmented") — "segmented" (default) or "underline".

Example:
```tsx
import { Tabs } from "@kalaa/react";

<Tabs
  variant="underline"
  items={[
    { value: "details", label: "Details", content: "Product details." },
    { value: "history", label: "History", content: "3 earlier versions." },
  ]}
/>
```

### Banner

Inline message in one of four tones; `warning` and `danger` are announced as alerts.

Props:
- `tone` (`"info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"`, required) — Meaning and colour. Warning and danger use `role="alert"`, the others `role="status"`.
- `title` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Bold first line.
- `actions` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Buttons on the right.

Example:
```tsx
import { Banner } from "@kalaa/react";

<Banner tone="warning" title="1 field needs attention">Fix the price before approving.</Banner>
```

### Badge

Small label with a tone (neutral, info, success, warning, danger). Status colours are for status only.

Props:
- `tone` (`BadgeTone`, optional, default: "neutral") — Colour meaning: neutral (default), info, success, warning or danger.

Example:
```tsx
import { Badge } from "@kalaa/react";

<Badge tone="success">Approved</Badge>
```

### StatusBadge

A Badge whose tone comes from a status word, in one mapping table: approved is success, needs review is warning, rejected is danger.

Props:
- `status` (`string`, required) — Status word such as "approved" or "needs review"; unknown words render neutral.

Example:
```tsx
import { StatusBadge } from "@kalaa/react";

<StatusBadge status="needs review" />
```

### ProgressBar

Progress of a task with a required label (visible or hidden) and a tone.

Props:
- `value` (`number`, required) — Current value.
- `max` (`number`, optional, default: 100) — Value that means complete (default 100).
- `label` (`string`, required) — Accessible name; shown unless `hideLabel`.
- `hideLabel` (`boolean`, optional, default: false) — Hides the label visually but keeps it for screen readers.
- `tone` (`"accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"`, optional, default: "accent") — Fill colour: accent (default), success, warning or danger.

Example:
```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from "@kalaa/react";

<ProgressBar label="Import progress" value={45} />
```

### Dialog

Modal dialog on Base UI with focus trap, Escape to close and a labelled close button. Sizes sm, md and lg (400, 560, 720px).

Props:
- `open` (`boolean`, optional) — Controlled open state.
- `defaultOpen` (`boolean`, optional) — Initial open state when uncontrolled.
- `onOpenChange` (`(open: boolean) => void`, optional) — Called when the dialog opens or closes.
- `trigger` (`ReactElement`, optional) — Element that opens the dialog (usually a Button).
- `title` (`ReactNode`, required) — Dialog heading; also its accessible name.
- `description` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Short explanation under the title.
- `footer` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Actions row, for example Cancel and Save.
- `size` (`"sm" | "md" | "lg"`, optional, default: "md") — Width: sm 400px, md 560px (default), lg 720px.

Example:
```tsx
import { Dialog, Button } from "@kalaa/react";

<Dialog
  trigger={<Button>Review import</Button>}
  title="Review import"
  footer={<Button variant="primary">Confirm</Button>}
>
  Twelve products are ready to import.
</Dialog>
```

### Table

Table component in @kalaa/react.

Props:
- `caption` (`ReactNode`, required)
- `hideCaption` (`boolean`, optional)
- `scrollLabel` (`string`, optional)

Example:
```tsx
import { Table } from "@kalaa/react";

<Table />
```

### DataTable

A sortable table for small record sets. The caller owns the rows, editor fields, validation, and persistence. Supply stable row IDs and give each editor control an accessible label.

Props:
- `caption` (`string`, required)
- `rows` (`readonly Row[]`, required)
- `columns` (`readonly DataTableColumn<Row>[]`, required)
- `getRowId` (`(row: Row) => string`, required)
- `getRowLabel` (`(row: Row) => string`, optional, default: getRowId)
- `newRow` (`() => Row`, required)
- `onCreate` (`(row: Row) => void | Promise<void>`, required)
- `onUpdate` (`(id: string, row: Row) => void | Promise<void>`, required)
- `onDelete` (`(id: string) => void | Promise<void>`, required)
- `emptyMessage` (`string`, optional, default: "No records")

Example:
```tsx
import { DataTable } from "@kalaa/react";

<DataTable />
```

### Pagination

Pagination component in @kalaa/react.

Props:
- `page` (`number`, required) — Current page, starting at 1.
- `pageCount` (`number`, required)
- `onPageChange` (`(page: number) => void`, required)
- `previousLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "Previous")
- `nextLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "Next")
- `emptyLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "No pages")
- `formatPage` (`(page: number, pageCount: number) => string`, optional, default: defaultFormatPage)

Example:
```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@kalaa/react";

<Pagination />
```

### Toolbar

Groups filters and actions while preserving ordinary Tab navigation.

Props:
- `actions` (`ReactNode`, optional)

Example:
```tsx
import { Toolbar } from "@kalaa/react";

<Toolbar />
```

### Meter

Meter component in @kalaa/react.

Props:
- `label` (`string`, required)
- `value` (`number | null`, optional) — Score from 0 to 100. A missing or invalid score is shown as unavailable.
- `unavailableLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "Unavailable")

Example:
```tsx
import { Meter } from "@kalaa/react";

<Meter />
```

### SuggestionReview

SuggestionReview component in @kalaa/react.

Props:
- `proposal` (`ReactNode`, required)
- `source` (`ReactNode`, optional)
- `score` (`{ label: string; value?: number | null }`, optional)
- `alternatives` (`readonly { id: string; label: ReactNode }[]`, optional, default: [])
- `alternativesLabel` (`string`, optional, default: "Ranked alternatives")
- `actions` (`ReactNode`, optional)

Example:
```tsx
import { SuggestionReview } from "@kalaa/react";

<SuggestionReview />
```

### Logo

The Kalaa square: a frame (the unlit moon) with a lit L-shaped crescent, plus an optional wordmark lockup. Colours follow `--kalaa-text` and `--kalaa-accent`, so it changes with theme and accent.

Props:
- `variant` (`"mark" | "lockup"`, optional, default: "mark") — "mark" is the square only; "lockup" adds the Kalaa wordmark.
- `size` (`number`, optional) — Height of the mark in px (the wordmark scales with it). Minimum 16 for the mark, 96px wide for the lockup.
- `title` (`string`, optional) — Accessible name of the mark. The lockup shows its own "Kalaa" text and ignores it.
- `mono` (`boolean`, optional) — Single-colour version: frame and corner both use currentColor.

Example:
```tsx
import { Logo } from "@kalaa/react";

<Logo variant="lockup" size={28} />
```

### CodeBlock

Monospace code with a Copy button. If the clipboard is unavailable it says to select the text and copy it.

Props:
- `code` (`string`, required) — The code to show and copy.
- `label` (`string`, optional, default: "Code") — Accessible name of the code region, for example "Install command".
- `language` (`string`, optional) — Hint for readers and tools, for example "bash" or "tsx". Not highlighted.

Example:
```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@kalaa/react";

<CodeBlock label="Install command" code="pnpm add ./vendor/kalaa-react-0.1.0.tgz" />
```

### Avatar

Compact identity badge showing an image or initials derived from `name`. Uses `--kalaa-radius-full` for circular user badges and `--kalaa-radius-md` (`shape="square"`) for workspaces or teams.

Props:
- `name` (`string`, optional) — Person or team name; used to derive up to two initials and as the accessible label.
- `initials` (`string`, optional) — Explicit initials override (for example "SR").
- `src` (`string`, optional) — Optional image URL; falls back to initials if omitted or if loading fails.
- `alt` (`string`, optional) — Accessible image description; defaults to `name`.
- `size` (`AvatarSize`, optional, default: "md") — Diameter: sm 24px, md 32px (default), lg 40px.
- `shape` (`AvatarShape`, optional, default: "circle") — True circle (`--kalaa-radius-full`, default) or theme-shaped square (`--kalaa-radius-md`).

Example:
```tsx
import { Avatar } from "@kalaa/react";

<Avatar name="Asha Rao" />
```

### Breadcrumbs

Hierarchical trail inside a `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` landmark, marking the final item with `aria-current="page"`. Supports client-side routing via `render` on each item.

Props:
- `items` (`BreadcrumbItem[]`, required) — Trail from root to the current page.
- `label` (`string`, optional, default: "Breadcrumb") — Accessible name for the `<nav>` landmark (default "Breadcrumb").

Example:
```tsx
import NextLink from "next/link";
import { Breadcrumbs } from "@kalaa/react";

<Breadcrumbs
  items={[
    { label: "Catalog", href: "/catalog", render: <NextLink href="/catalog" /> },
    { label: "Imports", href: "/catalog/imports", render: <NextLink href="/catalog/imports" /> },
    { label: "Batch #1042" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Combobox

Searchable single-value dropdown built on Base UI Combobox. Filters options as you type and supports full keyboard navigation (Arrow keys, Enter, Escape).

Props:
- `options` (`ComboboxOption[]`, required) — Choices as value and label pairs.
- `value` (`string | null`, optional) — Controlled selected value.
- `defaultValue` (`string | null`, optional) — Initial value when uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange` (`(value: string | null) => void`, optional) — Called when the selected value changes.
- `emptyMessage` (`string`, optional, default: "No matching options") — Message shown when no option matches the search query.
- `size` (`"sm" | "md"`, optional, default: "md") — Height: sm 30px, md 36px (default).
- `invalid` (`boolean`, optional) — Marks the control invalid.

Example:
```tsx
import { Combobox } from "@kalaa/react";

<Combobox
  aria-label="Catalog category"
  options={[
    { value: "beverages", label: "Beverages & Roasters" },
    { value: "spices", label: "Whole & Ground Spices" },
  ]}
  defaultValue="beverages"
/>
```

### Divider

1px rule in `--kalaa-border` with `role="separator"`. Supports horizontal rules (with an optional centred label) and vertical rules for toolbars.

Props:
- `orientation` (`DividerOrientation`, optional, default: "horizontal") — Axis: horizontal (default) or vertical (for toolbar and inline groups).
- `label` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Optional inline text centred on a horizontal divider.
- `decorative` (`boolean`, optional, default: false) — Hides the separator from the accessibility tree (`role="none"`).

Example:
```tsx
import { Divider } from "@kalaa/react";

<Divider label="Import options" />
```

### DropZone

Drag-and-drop and click-to-browse file target with `accept` filtering and a built-in `maxSizeBytes` size-limit notice and validation message.

Props:
- `label` (`ReactNode`, optional, default: "Drop a file here, or click to browse") — Primary prompt inside the drop target.
- `description` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Secondary instructions below the prompt.
- `accept` (`string`, optional) — Accepted MIME types or extensions (for example ".csv,text/csv").
- `maxSizeBytes` (`number`, optional) — Maximum file size in bytes; displays a size-limit message and rejects larger files.
- `multiple` (`boolean`, optional, default: false) — Allows selecting more than one file at once.
- `disabled` (`boolean`, optional, default: false) — Disables clicking and dropping.
- `onFiles` (`(files: File[]) => void`, optional) — Called with accepted files after a drop or file-picker selection.
- `onReject` (`(reason: string, file: File) => void`, optional) — Called when a file is rejected (size limit exceeded or type mismatch).

Example:
```tsx
import { DropZone } from "@kalaa/react";

<DropZone
  label="Drop a product CSV here, or click to browse"
  description="UTF-8 comma-separated values with a header row."
  accept=".csv,text/csv"
  maxSizeBytes={5 * 1024 * 1024}
  onFiles={(files) => console.log(files)}
/>
```

### Icon

Curated 24-icon set for operational interfaces: inline 24×24 SVG strokes using `currentColor`. Decorative by default (`aria-hidden="true"`); pass `label` when the icon stands alone without text.

Props:
- `name` (`IconName`, required) — Which icon to draw.
- `size` (`IconSize`, optional, default: "md") — Size: sm 16px, md 20px (default), lg 24px.
- `label` (`string`, optional) — Accessible name for an icon that stands alone. Omit it for decorative icons next to text (they are hidden from screen readers).

Example:
```tsx
import { Icon, Button } from "@kalaa/react";

<Button iconStart={<Icon name="upload" size="sm" />}>Import CSV</Button>
```

### Link

Inline text link in the accent colour, always underlined so it does not rely on colour alone. Pass `render={<NextLink href="..." />}` for client-side routing in Next.js.

Props:
- `render` (`useRender.RenderProp`, optional) — Replaces the `<a>` element, for client-side routing. Pass your router's link, for example `render={<NextLink href="/products" />}` with `next/link`. Kalaa props and classes are merged onto it.

Example:
```tsx
import NextLink from "next/link";
import { Link } from "@kalaa/react";

<p>
  See the <Link render={<NextLink href="/imports" />}>import history</Link> for row-level errors.
</p>
```

### Menu

Action menu on Base UI Menu with full keyboard support (Arrow keys, Home/End, type-ahead, Enter/Space, Escape). Pass an `items` array or compose with `Menu.Item` and `Menu.Separator`.

Props:
- `trigger` (`ReactElement`, required) — Button or element that opens the menu.
- `items` (`MenuEntry[]`, optional) — Declarative list of menu items and separators (alternatively pass `Menu.Item` children).
- `open` (`boolean`, optional) — Controlled open state.
- `defaultOpen` (`boolean`, optional) — Initial open state when uncontrolled.
- `onOpenChange` (`(open: boolean) => void`, optional) — Called when the menu opens or closes.
- `align` (`"start" | "center" | "end"`, optional, default: "start") — Alignment along the trigger edge (default "start").

Example:
```tsx
import { Menu, Button } from "@kalaa/react";

<Menu
  trigger={<Button>Row actions</Button>}
  items={[
    { label: "Duplicate record", onSelect: () => {} },
    { type: "separator" },
    { label: "Delete record", tone: "danger", onSelect: () => {} },
  ]}
/>
```

### MultiSelect

Searchable multi-value picker on Base UI Combobox (`multiple`), rendering selected values as removable chips inside the control. Designed to replace 20-checkbox lists inside table and column-mapping rows.

Props:
- `options` (`MultiSelectOption[]`, required) — Choices as value and label pairs.
- `value` (`string[]`, optional) — Controlled array of selected option values.
- `defaultValue` (`string[]`, optional, default: []) — Initial selected option values when uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange` (`(value: string[]) => void`, optional) — Called whenever the selected values array changes.
- `emptyMessage` (`string`, optional, default: "No matching options") — Message shown when no option matches the search query.
- `invalid` (`boolean`, optional) — Marks the control invalid.

Example:
```tsx
import { MultiSelect } from "@kalaa/react";

<MultiSelect
  aria-label="Mapped source columns"
  options={[
    { value: "sku", label: "SKU code" },
    { value: "ean", label: "EAN-13 barcode" },
    { value: "title", label: "Product title" },
  ]}
  defaultValue={["sku", "title"]}
/>
```

### Popover

Anchored non-modal overlay built on Base UI Popover for filter controls, quick inspectors or rich explanations.

Props:
- `trigger` (`ReactElement`, optional) — Element that opens the popover on click (usually a Button).
- `title` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Optional heading inside the popover.
- `description` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Optional supporting copy under the heading.
- `open` (`boolean`, optional) — Controlled open state.
- `defaultOpen` (`boolean`, optional) — Initial open state when uncontrolled.
- `onOpenChange` (`(open: boolean) => void`, optional) — Called when the popover opens or closes.
- `side` (`PopoverSide`, optional, default: "bottom") — Preferred side relative to the trigger (default "bottom").
- `align` (`PopoverAlign`, optional, default: "start") — Alignment along the side (default "start").

Example:
```tsx
import { Popover, Button } from "@kalaa/react";

<Popover
  trigger={<Button>Filter columns</Button>}
  title="Column visibility"
  description="Choose which fields appear in the table."
>
  <div>SKU, Title, Status</div>
</Popover>
```

### AppearanceMenu

Anchored appearance picker built from Kalaa `Popover` and `RadioGroup` for switching theme (`auto`, `light`, `dark`), accent colour (`neel`, `geru`, `mayur`) and corners (`square`, `soft`). Persists under the `"kalaa.theme"` `localStorage` key and syncs across tabs and `<kalaa-theme-picker>`.

Props:
- `label` (`string`, optional, default: "Appearance") — Trigger button and popover heading label (default "Appearance").
- `side` (`PopoverSide`, optional, default: "bottom") — Preferred popover side relative to the trigger (default "bottom").
- `align` (`PopoverAlign`, optional, default: "start") — Alignment along the popover side (default "start").
- `open` (`boolean`, optional) — Controlled popover open state.
- `defaultOpen` (`boolean`, optional) — Initial popover open state when uncontrolled.
- `onOpenChange` (`(open: boolean) => void`, optional) — Called when the popover opens or closes.
- `triggerVariant` (`ButtonVariant`, optional, default: "ghost") — Visual variant of the trigger button (default "ghost").
- `triggerSize` (`ButtonSize`, optional, default: "sm") — Size of the trigger button (default "sm").
- `onAppearanceChange` (`(appearance: Appearance) => void`, optional) — Called when the user changes theme, accent or corner shape.

Example:
```tsx
import { AppearanceMenu } from "@kalaa/react";

<AppearanceMenu />
```

### RadioGroup

Mutually exclusive choice list built on Base UI RadioGroup, with arrow-key roving focus and optional per-option descriptions. Always uses `--kalaa-radius-full` so radio buttons remain circular in both square and soft shape themes.

Props:
- `options` (`RadioOption[]`, required) — Choices in the radio group.
- `value` (`string`, optional) — Controlled selected value.
- `defaultValue` (`string`, optional) — Initial selected value when uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange` (`(value: string) => void`, optional) — Called when the selected radio changes.
- `orientation` (`"vertical" | "horizontal"`, optional, default: "vertical") — Layout direction: vertical (default) or horizontal.
- `disabled` (`boolean`, optional) — Disables every option in the group.
- `name` (`string`, optional) — Form field name.
- `required` (`boolean`, optional) — Marks a selection required in forms.

Example:
```tsx
import { RadioGroup } from "@kalaa/react";

<RadioGroup
  aria-label="Import mode"
  defaultValue="merge"
  options={[
    { value: "merge", label: "Merge with existing products" },
    { value: "append", label: "Insert new products only" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Skeleton

Layout placeholder shown while records or cards load. Decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); pulses gently and stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Props:
- `variant` (`SkeletonVariant`, optional, default: "text") — Shape preset: text line (default), rectangular block, or true circle (avatar placeholder).
- `width` (`number | string`, optional) — CSS width (number in px or string such as "60%").
- `height` (`number | string`, optional) — CSS height (number in px or string).

Example:
```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@kalaa/react";

<div aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading product">
  <Skeleton variant="text" width="40%" />
  <Skeleton variant="block" />
</div>
```

### Slider

Single-thumb range control on Base UI Slider with tabular readout and keyboard support (Arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up/Down). Track uses `--kalaa-radius-pill` and the thumb uses `--kalaa-radius-full`.

Props:
- `label` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Visible label associated with the slider thumb.
- `value` (`number`, optional) — Controlled numeric value.
- `defaultValue` (`number`, optional, default: 0) — Initial value when uncontrolled (default 0).
- `onValueChange` (`(value: number) => void`, optional) — Called as the slider thumb moves.
- `min` (`number`, optional, default: 0) — Minimum value (default 0).
- `max` (`number`, optional, default: 100) — Maximum value (default 100).
- `step` (`number`, optional, default: 1) — Step increment (default 1).
- `showValue` (`boolean`, optional, default: Boolean(label)) — Shows the formatted numeric value opposite the label (default true when `label` is set).
- `format` (`Intl.NumberFormatOptions`, optional) — Number format options passed to `Intl.NumberFormat`.
- `disabled` (`boolean`, optional) — Disables interaction.
- `name` (`string`, optional) — Form field name.

Example:
```tsx
import { Slider } from "@kalaa/react";

<Slider label="Minimum match confidence" defaultValue={80} min={0} max={100} step={5} />
```

### Spinner

Indeterminate activity ring using `currentColor` and `--kalaa-radius-full`. Announces `role="status"` with a visually hidden label unless marked `decorative` (as inside `Button loading`).

Props:
- `size` (`SpinnerSize`, optional, default: "md") — Diameter: sm 12px, md 16px (default), lg 24px.
- `label` (`string`, optional, default: "Loading") — Accessible text announced to screen readers (`role="status"`). Ignored when `decorative`.
- `decorative` (`boolean`, optional, default: false) — Hides the spinner from assistive tech; use when the surrounding control already says it is busy.

Example:
```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@kalaa/react";

<Spinner label="Validating import rows" />
```

### Stat

Single operational metric with a sentence-case label, tabular figure, optional status delta and comparison help line.

Props:
- `label` (`ReactNode`, required) — Metric name in sentence case (for example "Products pending review").
- `value` (`ReactNode`, required) — Primary figure, rendered in tabular numerals.
- `delta` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Optional change indicator (for example "+14%" or "-3 rows").
- `deltaTone` (`StatDeltaTone`, optional, default: "neutral") — Meaning of the delta badge: neutral (default), success, warning or danger.
- `help` (`ReactNode`, optional) — Secondary context or comparison period below the value.

Example:
```tsx
import { Stat } from "@kalaa/react";

<Stat
  label="Products approved"
  value="1,284"
  delta="+6.4%"
  deltaTone="success"
  help="Compared with the previous 7 days"
/>
```

### Toast

Transient status notification stack built on Base UI Toast (`ToastProvider` + `useToast()`). Mount `ToastProvider` once near the root of your app and trigger notifications with `const { toast } = useToast()`.

Example:
```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast, Button } from "@kalaa/react";

function SaveButton() {
  const { toast } = useToast();
  return (
    <Button onClick={() => toast({ title: "Catalog saved", tone: "success" })}>
      Save
    </Button>
  );
}

<ToastProvider>
  <SaveButton />
</ToastProvider>
```

### Tooltip

Brief non-interactive hint on Base UI Tooltip that appears on hover or keyboard focus and dismisses with Escape.

Props:
- `content` (`ReactNode`, required) — Brief label or keyboard shortcut shown inside the tooltip.
- `children` (`ReactElement`, required) — Focusable trigger element (for example a Button).
- `open` (`boolean`, optional) — Controlled open state.
- `defaultOpen` (`boolean`, optional) — Initial open state when uncontrolled.
- `onOpenChange` (`(open: boolean) => void`, optional) — Called when the tooltip opens or closes.
- `side` (`TooltipSide`, optional, default: "top") — Preferred side relative to the trigger (default "top").
- `delay` (`number`, optional, default: 250) — Hover delay in milliseconds before opening (default 250).
- `className` (`string`, optional) — Additional class name on the popup element.

Example:
```tsx
import { Tooltip, Button } from "@kalaa/react";

<Tooltip content="Export filtered rows as UTF-8 CSV">
  <Button>Export CSV</Button>
</Tooltip>
```
